book_title: On the Nature and Excellence of the Virtue of Abandonment
chapter_title: The Nature and Excellence of the Duty of the Present Moment

sections.title: The Divine Action Operates in All Things and at Every Moment
paragraphs: God speaks today as He spoke to our fathers, when there were neither spiritual directors nor any method of prayer. All that was required was that each one should attend to the voice of the divine word. The spiritual life was not an art; it was a life, a reality.

The divine action does not cease to flow throughout the universe. It fills all things, it creates and animates them, it preserves them, it leads them to their perfection. If the veil which covers our eyes were removed, we should see God working unceasingly around us and in us, giving life to our souls, arranging every event, and imparting grace through every breath we draw.

Nothing happens in this world except by the will or permission of God. He is the author of all that is good, and the sovereign orderer of all that is painful. In every event, however small or seemingly accidental, there is an operation of the divine power, offering itself to our acceptance.
Happy is the soul that recognizes this truth! For such a soul, the world is no longer an empty desert, nor an arena of blind chance, but the house of God and the gate of heaven.

sections.title: The Duty of the Present Moment as the True Source of Holiness
paragraphs: Sanctity is not a thing that is difficult of attainment. It consists in one single thing: fidelity to the order of God. And this fidelity is equally possible to all, whether in high station or in the lowest condition, in health or in illness, in great undertakings or in the humblest household duties.

The duty of the present moment is the ambassador of God, declaring His will to us. What is the duty of the present moment? It is whatever we are called upon to do, to bear, or to suffer at this very instant. The present moment is ever full of infinite treasures; it contains greater riches than you could possibly grasp.

Faith does not require that we should see the whole path laid out before us. It asks only that we take the single step that presents itself now. When you fulfill the duty of this passing moment with a pure intention, you are doing all that God requires of you; you are practicing the highest virtue.
Why do we torment ourselves looking for holiness in faraway places, in rare books, or in extraordinary practices, when it is right before our eyes, enclosed within the circle of our daily duties?

sections.title: Sanctity Does Not Consist in Extraordinary Gifts
paragraphs: Let us not be deceived by the dazzle of extraordinary deeds. A soul may perform miracles, prophesy, fast continuously, and spend nights in contemplation, and yet possess very little true charity if it seeks itself in these things.

True holiness is humble, simple, and silent. It does not consist in doing things that are great in the eyes of men, but in doing ordinary things with extraordinary love for God. The soul that sweeps a room or washes a dish out of love for the divine will is performing an act as holy as the contemplation of the angels.

All that God asks of us is our consent, our passive yielding to His active molding. The clay does not dictate to the potter the shape it shall take; it merely yields to the touch of his hands. So must we yield ourselves to the divine will in every circumstance.

sections.title: The Simplicity of the Way of Abandonment
paragraphs: The way of abandonment is so simple that the clever and the prudent of this world often pass it by with disdain. They look for complex theories and elaborate spiritual systems, thinking that to become holy one must read countless treatises and master intricate disciplines.

Yet Jesus said: 'I thank Thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.' The way of abandonment is the way of the child who rests securely in its mother's arms, untroubled by what tomorrow may bring.

O blind mortals, why do you wear yourselves out with anxiety? Yield to God. Let Him be God in you. Cast all your cares upon Him, for He careth for you. In this single act of surrender lies the peace that passeth all understanding.

book_title: On the Nature and Excellence of the Virtue of Abandonment
chapter_title: The Divine Action Concealed Beneath Humble Appearances

sections.title: The Sacrament of the Present Moment
paragraphs: The present moment is like an incarnation of the divine will. Just as God concealed His infinite majesty beneath the frail flesh of the Infant Jesus in the manger of Bethlehem, so He conceals His infinite love and wisdom beneath the humble accidents of our daily life.

Every moment is a sacrament in which God gives Himself to the soul that is ready to receive Him. The duties of our state, the interruptions of our work, the little contradictions of temperament in those around us, the changes in the weather, our bodily weariness—all these are the garments in which God wraps Himself.

If we had the eyes of faith, we should bow down in adoration before every creature and every event, saying: 'Truly God is in this place, and I knew it not.' The sacred bread of God's will is broken and distributed to us in every tick of the clock.

sections.title: The Eyes of Faith Versus Natural Sight
paragraphs: Natural sight sees only the outward shell; faith penetrates to the divine center. To the natural man, an illness is merely a misfortune, an insult is an outrage, a disappointment is a failure, and an interruption is a nuisance.

To the soul enlightened by faith, however, these very things are gifts sent from the throne of God. They are heavenly medicines for our spiritual pride, chisel-strokes of the divine sculptor shaping the image of Christ in us.

When we look at the tapestry of life from the back, we see only tangled threads, confused knots, and discordant colors. But when it is turned over, we see the exquisite masterpiece created by the Weaver. Abandonment is the act of trusting the Weaver even while we can see only the reverse side of the cloth.

sections.title: The Living Word Spoken in Daily Events
paragraphs: Scripture is the inspired word of God written once for all ages. But the divine will is also a living word that God speaks to us personally, hour by hour, in the events of our life. The events of life are God's letters to us.

When an unexpected trouble falls upon you, do not read only the signature of the human messenger who brought it. Read through it to the signature of the Almighty Father who permitted it for your sanctification.
Nothing reaches you without having passed through the loving scrutiny of God. He weighs every burden, measures every trial, and provides the exact portion of grace required for each instant.

sections.title: The Order of God as the Substance of Life
paragraphs: The order of God is the true substance of all that happens to us. Everything else is only shadow and appearance. The person who seeks God's order possesses everything, because in that order God Himself is found.

If you possess God, what does it matter whether you are rich or poor, praised or blamed, successful or defeated? The soul that has found rest in the order of God is like a rock in the midst of a tempestuous ocean: the waves dash against it, but it remains unmoved.
Offer to God your continuous 'Fiat'—'Let it be done unto me according to Thy word.' In that one word of consent, the soul finds perfect peace and invincible strength.

book_title: On the Nature and Excellence of the Virtue of Abandonment
chapter_title: How God Instructs the Soul in Every Event

sections.title: The Unwritten Gospel of Daily Providence
paragraphs: God continues to write His gospel in the lives of the faithful. Each generation, each soul, is a new page on which the Holy Spirit writes the mysteries of Christ. We are the epistles of Christ, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God.

Do not envy the saints of past ages who lived in the presence of miraculous signs and visions. You have at this very moment the same God, operating with the same infinite power and tenderness in the ordinary events of your day.
The soul that is attentive to the divine action needs no extraordinary revelations. It finds in the simplest occurrence a teacher of heavenly wisdom.

sections.title: The Food of the Soul: The Will of the Father
paragraphs: Our Lord Jesus Christ said: 'My meat is to do the will of Him that sent Me, and to finish His work.' This is also the only true food of our souls.

When we seek our own will, we feed upon ashes and wind. We may obtain what we longed for, but our soul remains hollow, restless, and unsatisfied. But when we accept the will of God, even in bitterness and sorrow, a secret sweetness and peace descend into our hearts.
The divine will is an inexhaustible spring of living water. Whoever drinks of this water shall never thirst again, for he carries within himself the fountain of eternal life.

sections.title: Deliverance from Perplexity and Future Anxieties
paragraphs: What is the cause of all our mental distress, our agonizing hesitations, and our sleepless nights? It is our persistent attempt to control tomorrow.

We want to foresee every danger, provide for every contingency, and arrange every outcome according to our own narrow wisdom. But we cannot see even a single second into the future. By worrying, we usurp a divine prerogative and load ourselves with burdens that God never intended us to carry.

Providence asks of you only the duty of the present moment. Leave tomorrow in the hands of Him who governs the stars. He who provides for the sparrow and clothes the lily of the field will not abandon you when tomorrow arrives.

sections.title: Resting in the Passive Operation of Grace
paragraphs: In the spiritual life, there is an active part and a passive part. The active part consists in fulfilling the commandments and performing the duties of our station. The passive part consists in receiving with loving resignation whatever God sends us.

The passive part is by far the more sanctifying and profound. In our active work, self-love can easily intrude, finding subtle satisfaction in our achievements and virtues. But in passive abandonment, self-love is starved, for the soul has nothing of its own to boast of.
Learn to let God work in you. Be quiet before the Lord, and wait patiently for Him. His touch is gentle, but His work is eternal.

book_title: On the Nature and Excellence of the Virtue of Abandonment
chapter_title: The Sublime Sanctity Found in Ordinary Faithfulness

sections.title: Mary and Joseph: The Models of Silent Fidelity
paragraphs: Consider the holy life of the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Joseph. What did they do that the world would consider great? They lived in a poor cottage in Nazareth; Joseph worked with the carpenter's plane, and Mary spun wool and prepared meals.

There were no sensational speeches, no public miracles, no grand institutions founded. Yet Mary is the Queen of Heaven, full of grace, because in every moment her soul breathed: 'Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum'—'Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done unto me according to Thy word.'
Her entire holiness was contained in that absolute, perpetual, loving abandonment to the divine will.

sections.title: True Greatness is Invisible to the World
paragraphs: The world judges by outward splendor, by titles, wealth, influence, and loud acclaim. God judges by the purity of the heart's surrender. Before the eyes of the Almighty, the patient endurance of a headache or a gentle answer to a harsh word is of greater value than the conquest of an empire.

Do not say: 'If only I had different health, if only I were in a different community, if only I had more leisure, I would become holy.' This is an illusion of the enemy. Your holiness is to be found right where you are, in the exact circumstances where God has placed you.
To flee from your present duties in search of some imaginary perfection is to run away from God while pretending to seek Him.

sections.title: The Universality of the Present Moment
paragraphs: The beauty of the sacrament of the present moment is that it is accessible to every soul, at any time, in any place. The prisoner in a dungeon, the sick man in a hospital bed, the mother caring for small children, the laborer in the field—all can practice abandonment with equal perfection.

It requires no money, no exceptional intellect, no journey to distant shrines. It requires only a loving heart that whispers: 'Lord, I want what You want, when You want it, how You want it, and for as long as You want it.'
When you have said that with complete sincerity, heaven is already opened in your soul.

sections.title: The Danger of Self-Invented Sanctity
paragraphs: Many souls spend their lives constructing their own spiritual ladders. They choose their own penances, invent their own crosses, and set up ideals that flatter their spiritual pride. But when God sends them a real cross—a humiliation, a delay, a sickness—they complain and kick against the goad.

The true cross is always the one that God chooses for us, not the one we choose for ourselves. The cross God chooses cuts right across our self-will, which is why it alone can crucify our pride and bring us into resurrection life.
Abandon your self-invented spiritual plans. Let God direct the course. He knows where you need to go, and He knows the shortest and safest road to get there.

book_title: On the State of Abandonment and Its Trials
chapter_title: The Inward Way of Faith and Darkness

sections.title: The Stripping of Sensible Consolations
paragraphs: When God intends to raise a soul to high sanctity, He almost always leads it through a dark and desolate way. He strips away the sweet feelings, the tears of sensible devotion, and the feeling of His immediate presence that had previously comforted the soul.
The soul feels abandoned, dry, cold, and incapable of any good thought. It cries out with the Psalmist: 'My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?'

Yet this very state, so terrifying to natural feelings, is the operation of God's deepest love. He withdraws His gifts so that we may learn to love the Giver rather than the gifts. He takes away the milk of infants so that we may feed upon the solid bread of the cross.

sections.title: Walking by Naked Faith Without Seeing
paragraphs: To walk by faith means to walk without seeing the path under our feet. It means placing our hand in the hand of God like a blind person, allowing Him to lead us through darkness, through fog, and along the edge of precipices.
Nature cries out for a light ahead; it wants assurance, certainty, and feelings of spiritual safety. But faith replies: 'I need no light except the knowledge that my Father is holding my hand.'
In the dark night of the soul, faith shines brighter than the noonday sun. It is a divine anchor cast into the invisible heart of God, which no storm can dislodge.

sections.title: The Illusion of Self-Direction
paragraphs: The greatest obstacle to God's work in us is our own human prudence. We are constantly calculating, reasoning, defending ourselves, and scheming to secure our own comfort and reputation.

All this frantic self-direction must be broken before God can take full possession of our faculties. We must become fools for Christ's sake, willing to appear weak, unskillful, and destitute of resources, so that the power of Christ may rest upon us.
When you no longer know what to do, do not panic. Stand still, be quiet, and look up to God. In that moment of complete helplessness, the angel of the Lord will appear to guide your steps.

sections.title: Consenting to the Divine Action in the Dark
paragraphs: Abandonment does not require that you should understand what God is doing. It requires only that you give your consent to what He is doing.

A patient undergoing a delicate surgical operation does not need to understand anatomy or the instruments the surgeon uses; he needs only to lie quiet and trust the skill of the physician. So the soul undergoing the spiritual surgery of divine purification must remain peaceful and quiet beneath the scalpel of Providence.

Every pang of sorrow, every interior desolation, is cutting away a tumor of pride or an attachment to self. Blessed is the soul that kisses the hand that wounds it, knowing that it wounds only to heal.

book_title: On the State of Abandonment and Its Trials
chapter_title: The Surrender of Self-Will and Human Prudence

sections.title: The Sacrifice of Our Own Plans
paragraphs: We form projects, sketch out beautiful futures, and set our hearts upon certain spiritual or temporal successes. Then a sudden storm breaks, a sickness intervenes, or an unexpected obstacle shatters our plans into pieces.

What is our first impulse? We grieve, we complain, we feel that everything is lost. But in reality, nothing is lost except our own self-will! God has merely overturned our small human plans to make room for His infinite divine plan.

Learn to hold all your plans with a light and open hand. When Providence says 'No,' let your answer be an immediate, unhesitating 'Amen.' The surrender of a cherished plan is a sweet sacrifice in the sight of God.

sections.title: The Power of the Fiat
paragraphs: 'Fiat'—'Let it be done'—was the word that called the universe into existence from nothingness. 'Fiat' was the word with which the Mother of God welcomed the Incarnation of the Word. 'Fiat voluntas tua'—'Thy will be done'—was the prayer of our Redeemer in the agony of Gethsemane.
When this word is pronounced from the bottom of a sincere and surrendered heart, it possesses a divine power. It changes trials into crowns, darkness into light, and weakness into heavenly fortitude.
Make this word the constant breath of your soul. Whatever happens, let your heart whisper: 'Fiat, Domine, fiat!' And the peace of God will instantly guard your heart and mind.

sections.title: Yielding the Helm to the Sovereign Pilot
paragraphs: As long as we keep our hands upon the helm of our life, trying to steer through the storms of existence by our own charts and compasses, we will be tossed about by fear and dread. We will tremble at every wave and despair at every dark cloud.
Take your hands off the helm. Step aside, and give the wheel to Christ, the Sovereign Pilot. He has steered through every tempest; He knows every reef and every hidden shoal.
When Christ is at the helm, the soul can sleep peacefully in the stern, even while the waves beat against the ship. For He who commands the winds and the sea is our Father and our Guardian.

sections.title: The Subtlety of Anxiety and Self-Love
paragraphs: Self-love is exceedingly crafty. When it cannot rule openly through worldly desires, it attempts to rule through spiritual anxiety. It causes us to worry about whether we are pleasing to God, whether our confessions were good enough, whether we are making progress, or how we shall endure future trials.
All this anxious self-examination is not true humility; it is pride disguised as piety. It is self-love grieving because it cannot find in itself something of which it can be proud.

True humility does not look at itself; it looks only at God. It acknowledges its nothingness with peace, casts all its sins into the ocean of divine mercy, and abandons itself wholly to the goodness of God.

book_title: On the State of Abandonment and Its Trials
chapter_title: Peace and Joy in the State of Abandonment

sections.title: The Unshakeable Fortress of Peace
paragraphs: There is a peace which the world cannot give, and which the world cannot take away. It is the peace of the soul that has abandoned all things to God.

What can harm the soul that wants only what God wants? If poverty comes, it says: 'Blessed be God for poverty.' If sickness comes, it says: 'Blessed be God for sickness.' If death comes, it says: 'Blessed be God who brings me to Himself.'
Such a soul is invulnerable. Its fortress is the will of God, and within those high battlements neither men nor demons can disturb its tranquility.

sections.title: Interior Calm Amidst External Storms
paragraphs: Look at the depths of the ocean: even when the most violent hurricane lashes the surface and creates towering waves, the waters a few fathoms below remain in absolute, motionless calm.

So it is with the abandoned soul. Outwardly, its body may suffer pain, its mind may be assaulted by temptations, and its worldly affairs may seem in total chaos. But deep in the center of the soul, where it dwells with God, reigns an inviolable, profound peace.

Do not be alarmed when the surface of your soul is troubled. Let the storm rage on the surface, but retire immediately to that secret sanctuary of your heart where God resides. There you will find quietness and assurance forever.

sections.title: Detachment from Spiritual Greed
paragraphs: There is a spiritual greed that is as dangerous as the love of money. It is the greed for spiritual consolations, heavenly visions, sweet experiences in prayer, and high spiritual status.

The soul that practices abandonment is detached even from these gifts. It accepts consolation with thanksgiving when God offers it, but it does not cling to it, and it does not lament when it is withdrawn.
To love God for His consolations is to love ourselves rather than God. But to love God in emptiness, in dryness, and in hardship is to love Him for His own sake, with a pure and disinterested love.

sections.title: Holy Indifference
paragraphs: Saint Francis de Sales and Saint Ignatius of Loyola spoke constantly of 'holy indifference.' By this they did not mean cold apathy or lack of feeling. They meant that supreme equilibrium of the will by which it desires only the glory of God and the fulfillment of His purpose.
The indifferent soul is like a balance that stands perfectly poised, ready to incline to whatever side the finger of God touches. It is ready for life or death, health or illness, honor or ignominy.
In this state of holy indifference, the soul attains true interior freedom. Nothing can enslave it, nothing can terrify it, for its treasure is in God, where no thief can approach nor moth destroy.

book_title: On the State of Abandonment and Its Trials

sections.title: The Crucible of Divine Love
paragraphs: Gold is refined in the furnace, and souls acceptable to God are refined in the furnace of humiliation and trial. The fire burns away the dross of self-love, self-seeking, and human attachment.
Do not flee from the crucible. When the fire burns hot, remember that the Goldsmith is sitting right beside the furnace, watching the flame with an eye of infinite tenderness.

He will never allow the heat to exceed the strength He gives you to bear it. And when He can see His own image clearly reflected in the molten gold of your soul, the trial will have fulfilled its work.

sections.title: Spiritual Dryness as Pure Love
paragraphs: When you feel dry and cold in prayer, and your mind wanders in spite of your efforts, do not give up in discouragement. Bring that very dryness to God as your offering.
Say to Him: 'Lord, I have nothing to give You today but this barren soil and this dry desert. But such as I am, I am entirely Yours.'

Such a prayer, uttered in the midst of spiritual desolation, is often more pleasing to God than the most eloquent words uttered in the warmth of consolation. It is pure love, offering everything and asking for nothing in return.

sections.title: Living in the Eternal Now
paragraphs: God is the Eternal Now: 'I AM WHO I AM.' He does not live in yesterday, nor in tomorrow, but in the timeless present. When we dwell in regret over the past, or in anxiety over the future, we depart from the place where God is.

Live in the present moment. Gather all the energy of your soul into this single hour, this single duty, this single breath. Yesterday is gone into the abyss of divine mercy; tomorrow is not yet born, and lies in the lap of divine Providence.
Only this moment is yours, and in this moment God is offering you His grace, His companionship, and His love.

sections.title: Perpetual Communion with the Divine Will
paragraphs: The consummation of the life of abandonment is a state of perpetual communion with God. The soul no longer needs long meditations or elaborate prayers to find its Lord; it finds Him in all things and all things in Him.
Every action becomes an act of worship, every sigh an incense of adoration, every trial a holy sacrifice. The soul lives in God and God in the soul.

Here, at last, the pilgrim has arrived at the haven of rest. The journey was through darkness and trials, but the end is light, joy, and peace without end. 'He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.'
